claims.text: Post-processing deep cryogenic treatment of additively manufactured HEA components reduces residual stresses.
Deep cryogenic treatment refines the microstructure of additively manufactured HEAs.
Deep cryogenic treatment improves the dimensional precision of additively manufactured HEA components.
Deep cryogenic treatment improves the mechanical integrity of additively manufactured HEA components.
Deep cryogenic treatment reduces fabrication-induced defects in additively manufactured HEA components.
As-built laser-additively-manufactured HEA components commonly exhibit residual stresses.
As-built laser-additively-manufactured HEA components commonly exhibit microstructural inhomogeneities.
Deep cryogenic treatment can be used as post-processing after laser melting deposition of a BCC HEA.
Deep cryogenic treatment should be applied immediately after additive manufacturing.
Immersion in liquid nitrogen followed by controlled warming is an effective DCT protocol for additively manufactured HEAs.
Deep cryogenic treatment reduces dislocation density in additively manufactured HEAs.
Deep cryogenic treatment refines grain boundaries in additively manufactured HEAs.
Deep cryogenic treatment increases phase homogeneity in additively manufactured HEAs.
Deep cryogenic treatment promotes atomic rearrangement that alleviates residual stress and microstructural defects.
A finer and more uniform microstructure produces lower dimensional distortion and enhanced mechanical properties.
DCT-treated laser-deposited HEAs will have greater tensile strength than untreated as-deposited material.
DCT-treated laser-deposited HEAs will have greater ductility than untreated as-deposited material.
The effects of DCT may vary with HEA composition, additive-manufacturing parameters, and the DCT protocol.
